title: Probate a will or qualify as executor or administrator
question: Someone has died and I am named executor, or there is no will. How do I probate the will or qualify as administrator in Charlottesville?
audience: families of people who have died
office: Clerk of the Charlottesville Circuit Court (Charlottesville Circuit Court, Clerk's Office, 16th Judicial Circuit)
summary: For someone who lived in the City of Charlottesville, wills are probated and executors or administrators appointed at the Charlottesville Circuit Court Clerk's Office, 315 East High Street. Call 434-970-3766 for an appointment. Bring the original will, a death certificate copy and asset values, and fill in the Probate Information Form (CC-1650). With no will, an heir can qualify; in the first 30 days only a sole heir or one with the others' waivers. You take an oath, give bond, file a list of heirs, and pay the state probate tax (10 cents per $100 on estates over $15,000), the city's one-third and a qualification fee. Within 30 days of qualifying or probate, send notice to the spouse, heirs and beneficiaries. Clerk's orders can be appealed within six months.

steps.step: Confirm that the Charlottesville Circuit Court is the right court
steps.who: The person holding the will, the named executor, or a family member
steps.how: Wills are probated, and administrators appointed, in the circuit court of the city or county where the person who died lived. If they lived in the City of Charlottesville, go to the Charlottesville Circuit Court Clerk's Office. If they lived in Albemarle County, use the Albemarle County Circuit Court, which is a separate court with its own clerk. Moving into a nursing home or similar institution because of age or ill health is presumed, unless shown otherwise, not to change where someone lived. With no known residence, use the court where their real estate lies, or else where they died or had property. Virginia has no separate probate court; usually the clerk or a deputy clerk, not a judge, handles probate.
steps.deadline: No set time frame; the court clerks' pamphlet recommends starting the initial steps within 30 days after death
steps.quote: A will shall be offered for probate in the circuit court in the county or city wherein the decedent has a known place of residence

steps.step: Until qualifying, the named executor only handles the funeral and protects the property
steps.who: The person named as executor in the will
steps.how: A named executor has no power to act for the estate until qualifying at the clerk's office. Before that, they may only arrange the burial, pay reasonable funeral expenses and keep property from being wasted. Keep the original will safe, because the original must be brought to the clerk.
steps.quote: A person named in a will as executor shall not exercise the powers of executor until he qualifies as such by taking an oath and giving bond in the court or before the clerk where the will or an authenticated copy thereof is admitted to record, except that he may provide for the burial of the testator, pay reasonable funeral expenses, and preserve the estate from waste.

steps.step: Check whether an executor or administrator needs to qualify at all
steps.how: Property owned jointly with survivorship rights, life insurance not payable to the estate, real estate passing by a transfer on death deed, and other property passing by contract or beneficiary designation is outside the probate estate. If the whole personal probate estate is $75,000 or less, at least 60 days have passed since the death, and no application to appoint a personal representative is pending or has been granted anywhere, all known successors can sign a Small Estate Affidavit (CC-1685), each signature notarized (or sworn before a clerk or deputy clerk), and give it to whoever holds a small asset such as a bank account, security, tax refund or item of personal property, without anyone qualifying. The affidavit states that any will was duly probated, so a will still has to be probated at the clerk's office; the clerk can probate a will without appointing anyone, and the person offering it then files the list of heirs and sends the notices (steps s10 and s12). If an heir, beneficiary or creditor does qualify on a personal estate of $35,000 or less, the inventory and accounts are waived unless there is real estate that person could sell (step s15).
steps.deadline: At least 60 days after the death (small estate affidavit)
steps.quote: this form should only be used when the value of the deceased person’s entire personal probate estate as of the date of death does not exceed $75,000.

steps.step: Call the Clerk's Office for an appointment
steps.who: The person offering the will, or the person asking to be appointed
steps.how: Call the Charlottesville Circuit Court Clerk's Office general line, 434-970-3766. Public hours are Monday through Friday, 8:30 am to 4:30 pm. The Clerk's Office is on the lower level of the Circuit Courthouse, 315 East High Street. The clerk may give you forms to fill in before the appointment.
steps.quote: You should telephone the Clerk’s Office for an appointment before you go to the courthouse.

steps.step: Fill in the Probate Information Form and gather what to bring
steps.who: The person offering the will, or the person asking to be appointed
steps.how: Fill in as much of the Probate Information Form (CC-1650) as you can; the clerk will help with the rest. Bring the original will and every codicil, a copy of the death certificate, and a list of the assets with values as accurate as you can make them. Count only the probate estate (see step s3).
steps.quote: Be sure to bring all originals of the will and any codicils with you when you come to the courthouse.

steps.step: Prove that the will was properly signed
steps.who: The person offering the will, with the will's witnesses if needed
steps.how: If the will has a self-proving affidavit (the testator and witnesses signed a sworn statement before a notary), no witness has to come. If it does not, bring at least one of the will's witnesses. For a will written entirely in the testator's handwriting, bring two disinterested people (not relatives, beneficiaries or relatives of beneficiaries) who know the handwriting; they swear to a Proof of Holographic Will (CC-1604) before the clerk or a deputy clerk (the same form serves for a will of a person in military service). A witness who lives outside Virginia, or cannot come because of sickness, age, legal confinement or another cause, can instead give a deposition before a clerk, deputy clerk or notary (or another officer authorised where the witness is): CC-1601 for a witness to a will without a self-proving clause, CC-1602 for a witness to a handwritten will. If the attesting witnesses have died, a person who knows their signatures and the testator's can prove them by deposition (CC-1603). The clerk may require all of the testator's will papers to be produced.
steps.quote: If a will has a self-proving affidavit, it is not necessary for any witnesses to come to the Clerk’s Office.

steps.step: If there is no will, or the named executor will not serve, work out who may be appointed
steps.who: Heirs (distributees), residuary or substantial beneficiaries, creditors
steps.how: With no will: in the first 30 days after death the clerk may appoint only a sole heir (or their designee), or an heir who brings written waivers (CC-1608) from all the other competent heirs. After 30 days, the first heir who applies may be appointed, but if more than one heir told the clerk within those 30 days that they mean to qualify, all of them must be given a chance to be heard first. After 45 days, a nonprofit charitable organization that was the decedent's conservator or guardian may be appointed after a diligent search for, and certified-mail notice to, any sole heir. After 60 days, a creditor or another person may be appointed after certifying a diligent search and a certified-mail notice to any sole heir at least 30 days before applying, or that no address could be found (CC-1609). If the will names no executor, or the executor refuses, fails to give bond, dies, resigns or is removed, a residual or substantial legatee under the will (or their designee) may be appointed administrator with the will annexed; if no such person applies within 30 days, a person who would have been entitled to administration if there were no will may be. The clerk must be satisfied that anyone appointed is suitable and competent, and cannot appoint a person under a legal disability (§ 8.01-2; for example a minor or an incapacitated person). An administrator of an estate without a will must also swear that they are not under a disability and have not been convicted of a felony of fraud or misrepresentation, robbery, extortion, burglary, larceny, embezzlement, fraudulent conversion, perjury, bribery, treason or racketeering; a sole heir with such a conviction may still be appointed if otherwise suitable and competent.
steps.deadline: No will: first 30 days after death, a sole heir or an heir with waivers; after 30 days, the first heir who applies; after 45 days, a nonprofit that was the decedent's conservator or guardian; after 60 days, a creditor or other person. Will with no serving executor: a residual or substantial legatee, then others if none applies within 30 days
steps.quote: After 30 days have passed since the decedent's death, the court or the clerk may grant administration to the first distributee, or his designee, who applies

steps.step: File the probate tax return and pay the state and city probate tax
steps.who: The person offering the will or asking for administration; the Clerk collects it
steps.how: If the estate is worth more than $15,000, file the confidential Probate Tax Return (CC-1651) with the clerk. Give the value of Virginia real estate (the local assessed value is accepted if you do not know the actual value) and a reasonable estimate of the personal property as of the date of death. Pay the state tax and the City of Charlottesville tax, which is one-third of the state tax, at the clerk's office; the clerk passes the city's share to the City Treasurer. No one can qualify until the tax is paid. If the later inventory shows a higher value, the clerk collects the extra tax.
steps.deadline: At the time the will is offered for probate or administration is sought
steps.fee: State: 10 cents per $100 of value or fraction of $100 (no tax on estates of $15,000 or less); City of Charlottesville: one-third of the state tax
steps.quote: No one shall be permitted to qualify and act as executor or administrator until the tax imposed by § 58.1-1712 has been paid.

steps.step: Take the oath and sign the bond
steps.who: The executor or administrator, before the clerk or a deputy clerk
steps.how: You swear to carry out the duties faithfully and sign a bond for at least the value of the personal estate (plus the real estate, or its rents and profits, if the will lets you sell it or receive them). Surety is required unless the will waives it or every heir or beneficiary is serving as personal representative; the clerk may also, in its discretion, accept a bond without surety when no more than $35,000 will come into your hands. The clerk will tell you whether a waiver applies. Surety is normally a surety bond bought from an insurance company and paid for from estate assets. A person who does not live in Virginia must file a written consent to service of process (CC-1610) and give bond with surety, unless a Virginia resident qualifies at the same time or the clerk waives surety under § 64.2-1411. Pay the qualification fee.
steps.fee: Qualification fee: $20 for estates up to $50,000, $25 up to $100,000, $30 over $100,000; no fee for estates of $5,000 or less. Any surety bond premium is extra.
steps.quote: The court or clerk shall require a personal representative to furnish security.

steps.who: The executor or administrator (or the person offering the will if no one qualifies)
steps.how: Sign the List of Heirs (CC-1611) under oath, giving every heir at law with address, relationship and age, whether or not there is a will. File it with the clerk when you qualify, and with the clerk of any other city or county where the decedent's real estate lies. You cannot be paid for your work until it is filed. If no one has qualified within 30 days of the death of a person without a will, an heir may file a list of heirs alone.
steps.deadline: At the time of qualification (or when the will is presented, if no one qualifies)
steps.fee: Recording cost is paid from the estate. When no will is probated and no administration is granted, recording a list of heirs costs a $25 state fee plus a $25 city fee.
steps.quote: furnish a list of heirs under oath in accordance with a form provided to each clerk of court by the Office of the Executive Secretary of the Supreme Court

steps.step: Get the probate order and certificate of qualification
steps.who: Clerk of the Charlottesville Circuit Court or a deputy clerk
steps.how: The clerk enters the order admitting the will and appointing you, and records the will. The clerk may issue a certificate of qualification, which has the same effect as formal probate or letters of administration and is your proof that you can act for the estate; if you ask, the clerk must make out the formal probate or letters. The clerk also gives you a written statement that you are responsible for filing tax returns and accounting for the estate, and copies of the notice form for the next step. Ask how many certified copies you need.
steps.fee: Copies: $0.50 per page; $2 for attaching the court seal and clerk's certificate (statutory amounts)
steps.quote: The court or clerk may issue a certificate of qualification to any personal representative for obtaining probate or letters of administration, which shall be given the same effect as the probate or letters made out in due form.

steps.step: Send notice to the spouse, heirs and beneficiaries
steps.who: The executor or administrator, or the person who probated the will
steps.how: Use the Notice Regarding Estate (CC-1616). Deliver it, or mail it first-class, to the surviving spouse, all heirs at law (even when there is a will), and the living beneficiaries under the will (including beneficiaries of any trust it creates) and under any earlier will probated in the same court, at their last known addresses. Anyone who signed a Waiver of Notice (CC-1618) does not need one, and neither does a non-heir whose gift is $10,000 or less of money or personal belongings; the law lists other exceptions, for example sending the notice to a guardian or conservator in place of the ward. The notice tells them they may ask for copies of the inventory and accounts. Anyone with an interest in the estate may give the notice.
steps.deadline: Within 30 days after the date of qualification or admission of the will to probate
steps.quote: Within 30 days after the date of qualification or admission of the will to probate, a personal representative or proponent of the will shall forward notice by delivery or by first-class mail, postage prepaid, to the persons entitled to notice at their last known address.

steps.who: The executor or administrator, or the person who probated the will
steps.how: Sign the Affidavit of Notice Regarding Estate (CC-1617), listing who was sent the notice and when, or stating that no notice was required, and record it at the Charlottesville Circuit Court Clerk's Office. The Commissioner of Accounts cannot approve the estate's settlement until it is recorded, and summons a fiduciary who has not done it after four months.
steps.deadline: Within four months (after qualification or probate)
steps.quote: The personal representative or proponent of the will shall record within four months in the clerk's office where the will is recorded an affidavit stating

steps.step: Record the will where any other Virginia real estate lies
steps.how: If the decedent owned, or left by will, real estate in another Virginia city or county, record a certified copy of the will at that circuit court clerk's office, and file the list of heirs there too. When there was no will, anyone with an interest in the decedent's real estate, including a qualified administrator, may record a Real Estate Affidavit (CC-1612) where the land lies, describing the land and naming the heirs; the clerk sends an abstract to the commissioner of the revenue so the land books can show the heirs.
steps.fee: Set by the clerk where you record. At the Charlottesville clerk, recording a list of heirs or a Real Estate Affidavit when no will has been probated and no administration granted costs the $25 state fee plus the $25 city fee; elsewhere the local $25 fee applies only if that locality has adopted it.
steps.quote: The personal representative of the testator shall cause a certified copy of any will or of any authenticated copy so admitted to record to be recorded in any county or city wherein there is any real estate of which the testator possessed at the time of his death or that is devised by his will.

steps.step: File the inventory with the Commissioner of Accounts
steps.who: The executor or administrator; reviewed by the Commissioner of Accounts appointed by the Charlottesville Circuit Court
steps.how: List the estate's assets at their value on the date of death on the Inventory for Decedent's Estate (CC-1670) and file it with the Commissioner of Accounts (the statewide directory lists commissioners by jurisdiction, or ask the clerk). Mail a copy to each entitled person who asked in writing for one. The commissioner charges a filing fee set by the court. The clerk compares the inventory with the probate tax return and collects any additional tax. Exception: if the personal estate passing by will or without a will is $35,000 or less and the person qualifying is an heir, a beneficiary, or a creditor whose claim exceeds the value of the estate, the clerk must waive the inventory and the accounts, unless the decedent owned real estate that person would have power to sell.
steps.deadline: Within four months after the date of the order conferring authority (qualification)
steps.fee: Commissioner of Accounts filing fee, set by the Charlottesville Circuit Court
steps.quote: Every personal representative or curator shall, within four months after the date of the order conferring his authority, return to the commissioner of accounts an inventory of all the personal estate under his supervision and control

steps.step: File accounts until the estate is settled
steps.how: File the first account (CC-1680) with the Commissioner of Accounts, covering the first 12 months, then an account for each later 12-month period until the estate is settled; you may file earlier, and the commissioner may extend a later deadline for reasonable cause. If all the heirs (no will) or all the residuary beneficiaries (will) are serving as personal representatives, you may instead file a Statement in Lieu of Settlement of Account (CC-1681) once all known charges are paid, six months have passed since qualifying and the residue has been delivered; if it cannot be filed by the account deadline, file an interim account or a sworn notice of intent by then. No accounts are needed when the clerk waived the inventory and settlement (step s15). Tell the commissioner at once if your address or phone number changes, and file the income, inheritance or estate tax returns the law requires.
steps.deadline: Within 16 months from the date of qualification; later accounts within four months after the end of each 12-month period
steps.fee: Commissioner of Accounts filing fee, set by the Charlottesville Circuit Court
steps.quote: Within 16 months from the date of the qualification, personal representatives shall exhibit before the commissioner of accounts a statement of all money and other property that the fiduciary has received, has become chargeable with, or has disbursed within 12 months from the date of qualification.

fees.quote: Unless a will has been probated or an administration granted on the decedent’s estate, a $25 fee shall be charged for the recordation of a list of heirs pursuant to § 64.2-509 or an affidavit pursuant to § 64.2-510, as provided in § 58.1-1717.1 and § 58.1-1718.

fees.item: Additional probate tax (or refund) after the inventory shows a different value
fees.amount: The difference; none charged or refunded if under $25
fees.quote: No additional tax shall be payable or no refund made if the payment or refund due would be less than twenty-five dollars.

fees.item: Copies of court papers (for example the will or the qualification order)
fees.quote: For making out a copy of any paper, record, or electronic record to go out of the office, which is not otherwise specifically provided for herein, a fee of $0.50 for each page or, if an electronic record, each image.

fees.item: Court seal and clerk's certificate on a copy (certified copy)
fees.amount: $2 (plus $0.50 if the judge's certificate is requested)
fees.quote: For annexing the seal of the court to any paper, writing the certificate of the clerk accompanying it, the clerk shall charge $2

fees.item: Surety bond premium (when surety is not waived)
fees.amount: Set by the surety company; paid from estate assets
fees.quote: This is normally done by purchasing a surety bond from an insurance company and paying for it out of estate assets.

fees.item: Commissioner of Accounts fees (inventory, accounts, statements in lieu)
fees.amount: Set by the Charlottesville Circuit Court; no Charlottesville schedule was found. The statewide guideline effective January 1, 2023 lists, for example, $135.00 to $350.00 for an inventory, $275.00 to $1,650.00 (plus .00075 over $1,000,000) for a first account by asset value, plus $5.00 for mailing, and $250.00 for a statement in lieu of settlement or a notice of intent to file one.
fees.quote: By statute, each Circuit Court sets the fees for its Commissioner(s) of Accounts

fees.item: Card convenience fee (only if the clerk accepts credit or debit cards)
fees.amount: A reasonable fee of no more than 4 percent of the payment or a flat $2 per transaction; whether the Charlottesville clerk takes cards was not confirmed
fees.quote: Such convenience fee shall not exceed four percent of the amount paid for the transaction or a flat fee of $2 per transaction.

escalation.trigger: A person interested in the probate of the will disagrees with the clerk's order, for example one refusing or admitting the will to probate or appointing the executor or an administrator
escalation.next: Charlottesville Circuit Court (a judge), which hears the matter anew (de novo)
escalation.deadline: Within six months after the clerk's order
escalation.quote: Any person interested in the probate of the will may appeal any order entered pursuant to § 64.2-444 within six months after the entering of such an order, without giving any bond, to the circuit court whose clerk, or deputy, has made the order.

escalation.trigger: More than one heir wants to be administrator
escalation.next: The clerk or the court, which must give every heir who gave notice an opportunity to be heard before appointing anyone
escalation.deadline: Notify the clerk during the first 30 days after the death
escalation.quote: more than one distributee notifies the court or the clerk of an intent to qualify after the 30-day period has elapsed, the court or the clerk shall not grant administration to any distributee, or his designee, until the court or the clerk has given all such distributees an opportunity to be heard.

escalation.trigger: The order of appointment in the statute would not serve the estate
escalation.next: Charlottesville Circuit Court, which may appoint another suitable person
escalation.quote: if the court determines that it is in the best interests of a decedent's estate, the court may depart from the provisions of this section at any time and grant administration to such person as the court deems appropriate.

escalation.trigger: The will's validity is doubtful or a dispute is expected before probate
escalation.next: Ask the clerk to summon everyone interested to show cause why the will should not be probated; the Charlottesville Circuit Court then hears the motion (with a jury if anyone interested asks)
escalation.quote: may request that the clerk of such court summon any person interested in the probate of the will to appear to show cause why the will should not be admitted to probate.

escalation.trigger: An interested person who was not part of the clerk's proceeding wants to contest the will, or to establish a will
escalation.next: Complaint to impeach or establish the will in circuit court (jury trial)
escalation.deadline: Within one year from the clerk's or court's order (two years if served only by order of publication)
escalation.quote: may file a complaint to impeach or establish the will within one year from the date of the order

escalation.trigger: An heir or beneficiary thinks the estate needs a bond with surety after surety was waived
escalation.next: Motion to the Charlottesville Circuit Court to require the personal representative to furnish security (a hearing is held)
escalation.quote: upon the motion of a legatee, devisee, or distributee of an estate, or any person who has a pecuniary interest in an estate, the court or clerk may require the personal representative to furnish security.

escalation.trigger: No affidavit of notice is recorded within four months after qualification
escalation.next: Commissioner of Accounts, who summons the fiduciary and enforces the filing
escalation.quote: If this subsection has not been complied with within four months after qualification, the commissioner of accounts shall issue, through the sheriff or other proper officer, a summons to such fiduciary requiring him to comply

escalation.trigger: An heir or beneficiary disagrees with the executor's or administrator's inventory or account
escalation.next: Object before the Commissioner of Accounts
escalation.quote: Any interested person, or the next friend of an interested person, may, before the commissioner of accounts, insist upon or object to anything

escalation.trigger: You disagree with the Commissioner of Accounts' report on an account
escalation.next: File exceptions; the Charlottesville Circuit Court examines them and corrects errors
escalation.deadline: File exceptions within 15 days after the report is filed in the clerk's office; with none filed, it stands confirmed the next day
escalation.quote: If no exceptions have been filed, the report shall stand confirmed on the day next following the expiration of the period of 15 days

escalation.trigger: A Commissioner of Accounts fails to perform, or violates, a statutory duty
escalation.next: Written complaint to the Standing Committee on Commissioners of Accounts of the Judicial Council of Virginia, sent to the Executive Secretary of the Supreme Court of Virginia
escalation.basis: Rules for Addressing Complaints Against Commissioners of Accounts (Judicial Council of Virginia, effective April 1, 2021), https://www.vacourts.gov/static/courts/circuit/resources/coa/coa_complaints.pdf
escalation.quote: All Complaints shall be submitted in writing to the Executive Secretary of the Supreme Court of Virginia

escalation.trigger: The Charlottesville Circuit Court enters a final order you believe is wrong
escalation.next: Court of Appeals of Virginia (notice of appeal)
escalation.deadline: Within 30 days from the date of the final order
escalation.quote: a notice of appeal to the Court of Appeals in any case within the jurisdiction of the court shall be filed within 30 days from the date of any final judgment order

escalation.trigger: You need a disability accommodation at the Clerk's Office, or one is refused
escalation.next: The Clerk of the Charlottesville Circuit Court; other complaints go through the Office of the Executive Secretary's ADA grievance procedure
escalation.quote: Complaints concerning a program, service, or activity of a circuit court clerk's office should be directed to that clerk.

caveats: No Charlottesville page describes probate. The Charlottesville Circuit Court page on vacourts.gov and the city's Circuit Court pages give only the Clerk's Office address, phone and hours. The steps come from state law and the statewide Office of the Executive Secretary forms and instructions, which note possible local variations. Local practice (appointment booking, documents, number of certified copies, accepted payment methods) was not found and should be confirmed by phone.

Venue matters here. A Charlottesville resident's will goes to the Charlottesville Circuit Court; an Albemarle County resident's goes to the separate Albemarle County Circuit Court, even though both courthouses are in Charlottesville.

The City Code text of §§ 30-396 and 30-397 is quoted from the ordinance attached to the City Council agenda for October 21, 2024 (CivicClerk). The approved minutes list it among the Consent Agenda items, which Council adopted 5-0, and do not mark it carried to a later meeting. The codified text on Municode was not read (its terms of use were not confirmed), and later amendments were not checked. The staff report says the city already levied the one-third tax before 2024; the 2024 change added the $25 local list-of-heirs and real-estate-affidavit fee.

Email: the vacourts.gov court page shows an obfuscated email address beside the elected Clerk's name, and the city page offers an email form for the named Clerk. These look like personal mailboxes, so neither is recorded. No general office mailbox for probate was found.

The 'Probate in Virginia' pamphlet (Virginia Court Clerks' Association, republished July 2019, hosted on vacourts.gov) gives a $50,000 limit for small-asset estates. Current Va. Code § 64.2-601(A)(1) and the CC-1685 Small Estate Affidavit (revised 07/26) say $75,000. The pamphlet's probate tax figures ($1.00 state and .33 local per $1,000) match 10 cents per $100 plus one-third.

The CC-1651 Probate Tax Return's preparation note says the form 'must be completed if the value of the estate exceeds $10,000', but the form itself and Va. Code § 58.1-1714 say $15,000. The statute governs.

Some statewide instructions are old: CC-1650 instructions are dated 07/03 and 07/13 and quote an earlier wording of the nursing-home presumption, and CC-1608 instructions cite repealed §§ 64.1-1 and 64.1-11 (now in Title 64.2).

Clerk fees: the Charlottesville clerk publishes no itemized probate fee list. The fees given are the statutory amounts. How the clerk applies recording fees to wills and lists of heirs, whether it charges the $3 bond fee in § 17.1-275(A)(6), and whether cards are accepted (if they are, § 17.1-275(A)(27) has the clerk collect a convenience fee of no more than 4 percent or a flat $2) were not confirmed.

Commissioner of Accounts: the Charlottesville Circuit Court's own commissioner fee schedule was not found. The amounts given are the statewide Uniform Fee Schedule Guidelines, which the vacourts.gov page says to confirm with the local circuit court. Commissioners are individual attorneys, so no names or contact details are recorded; use the statewide directory or ask the clerk.

Not covered in detail: administrators appointed only for wrongful death or personal injury suits (§ 64.2-454), curators (§ 64.2-451), corporate fiduciaries, foreign (out-of-state) probate and authenticated copies (§ 64.2-450), estate debts and creditor claims, and federal or state income and estate tax returns, and notice to creditors (forms CC-1686 and CC-1687 on the fiduciary forms page).

§ 64.2-445 gives the six-month appeal of a clerk's order to a 'person interested in the probate of the will'. How it applies to a clerk's appointment of an administrator when there is no will was not confirmed; for that, ask the clerk or a lawyer (the court may also depart from the order of appointment, § 64.2-502(B)).

The CC-1650 instructions and the clerks' pamphlet do not mention the 45-day rule for a nonprofit conservator or guardian (§ 64.2-502(A)(3)), the clerk's discretion to waive surety for estates of $35,000 or less (§ 64.2-1411), or the waiver of inventory and accounts for personal estates of $35,000 or less (§ 64.2-1302); those come from the statutes only, and how the Charlottesville clerk applies them was not confirmed.

corrections: All 85 original quotes confirmed. The 72 state-law quotes are substrings of I.text_of for the cited section (whitespace normalised only), each in the cited subsection. The 13 local and procedure quotes were found word for word in the official sources, re-fetched read-only on 2026-10-11: the CC-1650 and CC-1685 instructions, the Commissioner of Accounts fee guideline and complaint rules, the Circuit Courts pamphlet, and the City Council packet for October 21, 2024. The approved minutes confirm item 12 passed on the 5-0 consent agenda vote and was not carried.

21 quotes added, each checked against I.text_of the same way: §§ 64.2-403(B), 64.2-447(A), 64.2-500(A) (30-day fallback), 64.2-502(A)(3) and (D) (felonies; sole-heir exception), 64.2-506 (formal letters), 64.2-508(A)(3) and (4), 64.2-510(A), 64.2-601(A)(2) and (3), 64.2-1302 (two), 64.2-1304(B), 64.2-1314(B) (two), 64.2-1411(A) (two) and 17.1-275(A)(27) (in legal_basis and as a new fee).

s6: the draft said a witness could give a deposition before a notary on CC-1601, CC-1602, CC-1603 or CC-1604. The forms show CC-1604 is not a deposition: two disinterested people swear to it before the clerk or a deputy clerk, and it also serves for a will of a person in military service. CC-1603 proves the signatures of attesting witnesses who have died. Rewritten from the forms, with § 64.2-447(A) and § 64.2-403(B) added.

s3: the draft left out one statement the Small Estate Affidavit requires, that no application to appoint a personal representative is pending or has been granted anywhere (§ 64.2-601(A)(3); line 7 of CC-1685). Added, together with: the affidavit covers small assets such as accounts, securities, refunds and personal property; signatures may be sworn before a clerk, deputy clerk or notary; and a proponent who probates without qualifying files the list of heirs and sends the notices.

s7: the draft said 'Anyone appointed ... must swear they are not under a legal disability or convicted of certain felonies'. § 64.2-502(D) sets that oath for administrators of estates without a will, so the step now says so, lists the felonies and gives the sole-heir exception. Also in s7: added the 45-day rule for a nonprofit that was the decedent's conservator or guardian (§ 64.2-502(A)(3)); restated the 30-day fallback for administration with the will annexed in the statute's terms (a person entitled to administration if there were no will, not 'a person who would inherit'); added the designee, and the executor's failure to give bond, death, resignation or removal; and used the statute's 'residual or substantial legatee'.

s9: the surety exceptions were incomplete. Added the clerk's discretion to accept a bond without surety when no more than $35,000 comes into the fiduciary's hands (§ 64.2-1411(A)), and named it as the waiver § 64.2-1426 allows for nonresidents. Bond amount now includes rents and profits of real estate, as § 64.2-504(A) says.

s15 and s16: added the waiver of inventory and settlement that the clerk 'shall' grant for personal estates of $35,000 or less when an heir, a beneficiary or a creditor whose claim exceeds the estate qualifies, with its real-estate exception (§ 64.2-1302). Also added the conditions for a Statement in Lieu (§ 64.2-1314(B)) and the interim-account or notice rule (§ 64.2-1314(C)), and that later account deadlines may be extended for reasonable cause and accounts may be filed early (§ 64.2-1304(B), (C)). The caveat saying the index has no text for § 64.2-1314 was wrong: row 29298 has it. That caveat was removed, and § 64.2-1411 was looked up.

s11: 'issues a certificate of qualification' changed to 'may issue', as § 64.2-506 says. Added that on request the clerk must make out formal probate or letters. Replaced the unsourced 'Banks and others accept it as proof' with the statute's same-effect rule.

s12: the notice list now includes beneficiaries of a trust created by the will and of an earlier will probated in the same court (§ 64.2-508(A)(3), (4)). Added the guardian or conservator exception (§ 64.2-508(B)(4)), and that anyone with an interest in the estate may give the notice (§ 64.2-508(F)).

s14: added the Real Estate Affidavit's legal basis (§ 64.2-510(A)), and the clerk's abstract to the commissioner of the revenue (§ 64.2-510(B)). The step's fee was null; it now gives $25 state (§ 58.1-1717.1) plus $25 city (City Code § 30-396) at the Charlottesville clerk when no will is probated and no administration granted, and says other localities charge the local fee only if they have adopted it (§ 58.1-1718 'may').
s1: the nursing-home presumption now covers similar institutions entered because of age or ill health, and says it can be rebutted (§ 64.2-443(B)).

Fees: added the card convenience fee cap (§ 17.1-275(A)(27)), with a note that card acceptance was not confirmed. To the Commissioner of Accounts item, added the guideline's $5.00 mailing charge and its $250.00 fee for a statement in lieu or a notice of intent, both read in the guideline PDF. The clerk-fees caveat no longer says the law 'allows' the convenience fee: the statute says the clerk 'shall collect' it.

Escalation: the § 64.2-445 rung now uses the statute's 'person interested in the probate of the will', and a caveat says its reach to appointments in estates without a will was not confirmed. The § 64.2-1212 rung now says exceptions are due within 15 days of filing, and that the report stands confirmed the next day if none is filed.
Summary: 'Notify heirs within 30 days' now says the notice goes to the spouse, heirs and beneficiaries, within 30 days of qualifying or probate.

Confirmed without change: the contacts (the city page gives the address, general line, hours and lower-level location; the vacourts.gov footer and the complaint rules give the OES address); the 18 form numbers, titles and URLs, against the fiduciary forms page; the CC-1651 $10,000 versus $15,000 note; the dates on the CC-1650 instructions and the repealed citations in CC-1608; the pamphlet's $50,000 figure and tax rates; the staff report; and the two phrases quoted inside caveats. No staff names, personal mailboxes or direct lines are recorded; the staff report, the court pages and the ADA notice name individuals, and none of those names were copied.
open_issues: Local practice is not published: appointments, accepted payment methods, the number of certified copies, and whether and how recording fees and the $3 bond fee (§ 17.1-275(A)(6)) are charged. Confirm with the Clerk's Office by phone.
City Code §§ 30-396 and 30-397 are quoted from the ordinance as adopted on October 21, 2024. The codified text on Municode and any later amendment were not checked.
No Charlottesville Commissioner of Accounts fee schedule was found. The amounts given are the statewide guideline.

Whether § 64.2-445's six-month appeal reaches a clerk's appointment of an administrator when there is no will was not confirmed. Neither was how the Charlottesville clerk applies the § 64.2-1411 surety waiver and the § 64.2-1302 inventory waiver.

For the appeal to the Court of Appeals, where the notice is filed and what else is required under the Rules of Court were not researched. Creditor claims and notice to creditors (CC-1686, CC-1687) are outside this file.
